_meta.note: Corpus for the Fase 5 Paso 0 measurement: does an LLM obey a glossary given as a prompt instruction as reliably as the literal string-replacement path? Small on purpose — this is a real-money A/B against a live API, not an exhaustive suite.

cases.source: 灰音、おはよう。今日も一緒に学校へ行こう。
アルテミスは本当に強い戦士だ。誰も彼女には勝てない。
せんぱい、待ってください!一緒に帰りましょう。
cases.note: honorific-style term, tests whether the model keeps a term the instruction says to keep verbatim rather than translating its meaning

cases.source: 桜花学園に着いたら、まず職員室へ行ってください。
cases.note: source===target 'keep unchanged' case — the exact VNDB no-op the plan calls out. This is the case literal replacement gets right by construction (a no-op) but that never proves the model would leave it alone on its own.

cases.source: 灰音とロゼは幼馴染で、いつも一緒にいる。
cases.note: two glossary terms in the same line

cases.source: アルテミスとせんぱいが桜花学園の前で話している。
cases.note: three terms mixing renderings and keep-unchanged in one line — the hardest case in this corpus

cases.source: 今日は誰も学校に来なかった。静かな一日だった。
cases.note: no glossary term present — negative control. The prompt leg's {glossary} block should render empty (collapsed line) here; compliance for a line with zero expected terms is trivially 'pass' and exists to confirm the negative control doesn't error, not to move the percentage.

cases.source: ロゼが灰音に手紙を渡した。中には短いメッセージが書かれていた。
cases.note: both names again in a different sentence structure, to avoid the corpus being a single sentence pattern repeated with names swapped
